Subject: Draft MAP: post-close implementation plan (rollout, canary, migration, training)

Hi Olivia / Mateo —

Great to be over the finish line on commercial terms. As discussed in our closing call, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan that embeds the post-signature implementation playbook (rollout phases, canary tests, migration windows, and training batches). Please treat this as a working document — the goal is alignment so we can lock in dates and owners by EOW.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm go-live window: target week of 2028-09-11 (can shift +/- 1 week)
- Approve the proposed canary cohort (10% traffic, two-week evaluation)
- Identify internal training stakeholders and preferred training dates
- Procurement: confirm final SOW signature path and expected DocuSign approver list

What's attached:
- Sunrise_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with timeline, owners, acceptance criteria) [Attachment]
- canary-test-plan.md (test scenarios, success metrics) [Attachment]
- training-schedule.pdf (proposed sessions & seat counts) [Attachment]

Suggested next steps:
1) You and your team review MAP and mark change requests directly in the sheet
2) We schedule a 30-min alignment call next week to finalize the canary cohort and runbook
3) Once agreed, Redwood will create a signed SOW and DocuSign packet

If it's helpful I can split the MAP into a separate Acceptance Criteria doc to make sign-offs more granular.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales

Diego —

Thanks for the draft and attachments. Quick notes from the Sunrise side after a rapid internal review:

- Go-live window: the week of 2028-09-11 is fine for Prod toggle but we need a hard freeze window from 2028-08-28 to 2028-09-08 for our regulatory team to complete final validation.
- Canary cohort: prefer an incremental canary (day 1 internal-only traffic, day 2–14 10% external). Can we add an option for a longer canary (3 weeks) if we need more metrics?
- Migration: we'll need a dry-run migration on 2028-08-21 (non-prod) with a checklist that includes data retention verification and API contract tests.
- Training: morning sessions are better for our R&D and late-afternoon for ops. Can you preserve two distinct cohorts?

I'll route the MAP to procurement now — procurement will add the required PO and internal approver list to the DocuSign packet. Attaching one small edit to the MAP (see row comments) and a note on the canary cadence.

Olivia

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: post-close implementation plan (rollout, canary, migration, training)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the feedback. Adding technical detail below that we'll fold into canary-test-plan.md and the MAP tab:

Canary plan (technical):
- Canary cohort definition: Phase A = internal pilot (support + dev), Phase B = 10% customer traffic routed via smart routing policy to canary cluster
- Duration: baseline 14 days with daily metric check-ins (latency P50/P95, error rate, model-output fidelity measured vs. golden prompts)
- Success gates (examples):
  - Error rate < 0.5% sustained over 72 hours
  - No production rollback required for non-functional regressions
  - Quality regression: automated evals on the nightly prompt suite show <= 2% drop in primary metrics
- Rollback: automated traffic shift back to previous model variant plus immediate hotfix window (2 hours)

Migration plan (dry-run):
- Non-prod dry-run: 2028-08-21 — full dataset subset, run migration scripts, validate schema & embeddings checks
- Final migration: 2028-09-09 (maintenance window) — cutover strategy is blue/green with fallback to pre-cutover snapshot

Training plan:
- Two cohorts: Ops (late afternoon, 2x 90-minute sessions), Engineers (mornings, 3x 60-minute deep dive)
- Training deliverables: runbooks, quickstart cheat-sheet, recordings, and a 30-day SLO/warmline support schedule

I'll update the canary-test-plan.md with the gate definitions and link a test-run checklist (will attach in next email).

Regards,
Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
